look_here_first: PASPALUM PUBIFLORUM: a complete flowering head often has several narrow one-sided racemes, with oval flattened green spikelets. The existing Beth photograph illustrates ONLY one section of a raceme, not the whole branch count. Check several mature spikelets approximately 2.7–3.2 mm and the upper-glume fine hairs to separate from broad large-spikeleted Florida paspalum and long-silky-haired dallisgrass. NEW REAL DIAGNOSTIC PHOTO SERIES: four archived Central Texas original Harms images now show the FULL set of unilateral racemes, reproductive tissue, a close-up spikelet row and real blade/sheath junction. Source labels and rights are explicit. Compare ripe, calibrated spikelet glumes with Florida paspalum and Dallisgrass; do not claim 2.7–3.2mm from an unscaled image or identify species from one branch.

learner_visual_status.note: Visible field lesson refined with locally archived original photos and specific true macro gaps. No county audit or unverified anatomy.

crew_field_steps: Find the tight vertical double-row appearance of the green oval spikelets on the visible raceme.
Identify the green leafy blade beside the head; the photographed finger gives coarse scale but is not a millimeter ruler.
Seek complete mature panicle, glume surface hair and collar ligule photos before distinguishing Florida paspalum, dallisgrass or others.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: LAST-MILE: one locally verified whole ROOTED P. pubiflorum plant with an intact same-plant flowering culm and ruler; the existing full flowering-head photo is a cut stem with two visible racemes, not roots.

LAST-MILE: mature individually isolated upper glume of P. pubiflorum under side lighting at 10–20× with a physical 1-mm scale; document actual fine hairs, veins and 2.7–3.2 mm spikelet dimensions before species-level micro arrows.

LAST-MILE: opened INNER blade–sheath junction with 1-mm ruler resolving the true ligule membrane edge and any attached hairs; the existing Harms collar photo shows the external junction, not a confidently measured membrane.
LAST-MILE COMPARISON: matched, mature and locally vouchered P. pubiflorum vs P. floridanum / P. setaceum spikelets at the same scale, with rooted habit and raceme count.

comparisons.key_distinctions: One cropped raceme never proves head branch count. A label saying 'paired' needs to show actual attachment at a node at enough resolution; the current oval row photo can't prove micro pubescence. Compare a single mature spikelet with P. floridanum and P. setaceum at 10–20×.
do_not_use_alone: Number of racemes without the entire flowering axis
Habitat, height, or vegetative tuft in isolation
Microscopic glume hairs or spikelet length inferred from a photo without scale
comparisons.field_identification_note: Shoot full ONE culm and all racemes, and detached mature spikelets with ruler. Backlit upper glume with true tiny hairs and a collar/ligule image remain unphotographed.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Hairyseed paspalum: full flowering culm → one-sided racemes → glumes → true leaf collar
steps: A complete cut flowering head, actual spikelet rows and external collar-region photo are NOW archived; obtain a same-plant rooted culm, isolated mature glume with mm ruler, and OPEN inner ligule before claiming full diagnostic photo completion.
First show the WHOLE head, then ONE one-sided raceme and attached spikelets. Never treat a photograph of one branch as total raceme count.
Obtain a real intact mature spikelet and measure it with 1-mm reference; use margin hair pattern and glumes to separate close Paspalum taxa.
Photograph blade/sheath joint and same-plant rootstock; knotgrass needs actually rooted horizontal stolons, not merely a low mat.
If plant photo is source-labelled only, keep identity tentative and leave existing county-native fields unchanged.
PHOTO 3: inspect a real complete flowering head and count all one-sided racemes on the SAME stem, not a crop of one row.
PHOTO 4: study actual flowering organs within the panicle; purple or yellow tissue is not a ripe caryopsis.
PHOTO 5: get a separately detached mature 2.7–3.2 mm spikelet and shine angled light on true glume hairs; picture has no reliable measured 1mm proof.
PHOTO 6: lift the blade and photograph the real membranous inner ligule with millimeter reference, avoiding hairs on nearby external sheath.
Compare to P. floridanum with larger published spikelet sizes and dallisgrass with long silky hairs; do NOT key on site moisture or gross head similarity alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: P. pubiflorum in accepted treatments commonly has 2–5(-7) unilateral racemes, small to medium 2.7–3.2 mm spikelets with glumes glabrous or minutely pubescent. Florida paspalum usually carries larger rounder spikelets; dallisgrass has conspicuous silky marginal hairs on larger spikelets; thin paspalum's varieties can differ dramatically in foliage hairs and smaller spikelets. Without a true scale, don't force it.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Gross photo structures are references, NOT expert confirmation. Even new licensed images are PROVISIONAL — USER PHOTO REVIEW PENDING and not proof of Hays County presence. Four Harms original images are copyrighted, permitted for scientific/educational use only WITH visible Bob Harms credit. No Creative Commons grant and no confirmed Hays voucher for each photo.

lane4_20261023.important_scientific_correction: Hairyseed paspalum does NOT uniformly have hairy mature spikelets. Flora of North America and Kew describe glabrous OR pubescent spikelets/upper glumes. Pubescence cannot be a required yes/no species filter.
lane4_20261023.crew_first_id: Find a often low-arching perennial flowering shoot with (2–)3–7 one-sided racemes; track rows of paired overlapping compressed ovoid spikelets and if possible decumbent culm rooting at nodes. Check the true membranous 1–3 mm ligule and mature ca 2.7–3.6 mm spikelets with actual calibrated ruler; compare P. floridanum's often larger ~4 mm spikelets, P. dilatatum's characteristically long silky glume hairs.
crew_teach_sequence: View actual whole panicle source Bob Harms PAPU5-I for raceme count (whole head only)
View small oval spikelets PAPU5-J1; photograph does NOT prove pubescence, glume veins or physical sizes
View true collar region PAPU5-L; open membrane and measure before drawing anatomical arrows
Compare equally ripe measured spikelets against Florida paspalum and Dallisgrass; don't identify solely from hairs

Actual opened membrane ligule 1–3 mm in junction with calibrated 1 mm bar, source-verified
